headline: Meta's Muse shopping agent filled four of its six typical product picks by browsing two websites live and only two from Meta's own catalog, according to a small test by the analytics firm Profound.
score_reason: Pool 4 lowered by 1: Profound published the research on 2 Oct 2026 and PPC Land reports it nine days later with no new test; it is a small vendor-run sample.
importance_line: Online shops that want Meta's agent to recommend their products need pages an AI can read, and shoppers may be steered by sites they cannot see, but this is one small, vendor-run test of a single retail category that no one has repeated, and Meta has published no comparable data.
summary: PPC Land reports on a research post that Profound, a company that tracks how AI tools describe brands, published on 2 Oct 2026: in a test of 50 prompts, a typical set of six recommendations from Meta's Muse shopping agent had four products from two merchant websites that Muse browsed live and two from Meta's product catalog, even though the catalog supplied about 15 times as many candidates. Profound also found that Muse and a rival agent, Instinct, browse without identifying themselves or naming their sources, which makes it hard for shops to see when an agent has visited; it calls its test a small exploratory sample, and it sells services that track AI agents on websites.
notes: Read PPC Land in full. Profound's own post (2 Oct 2026) was not opened; PPC Land is the secondary report, so the credit names both. Older research re-reported on 11 Oct 2026; PPC Land adds analysis and caveats but no new test.
